current_round.prompt:
Make human acceptance, rejection, cancellation, failure and recovery measurable from durable Goal history.

The request remains valid, but its description of every passed Quality/Governance gate reaching Done is outdated. Current Skills run checks, integration leads to Review, and approval is a separate decision. Passing a Skill, or having no required check Skills, must never be counted as human acceptance. Round 1 has substantial uncommitted work but no candidate or completed verification; reassess it against current lifecycle and Skill execution code.

Record immutable human decision events with a stable identity, Goal, Round, node, reviewer, decision time, accepted or rejected result, optional reason and exact candidate. Make rejection a supported outcome distinct from cancellation, with an explicit path to a new Round that retains the rejection. Record terminal outcomes with completion time, resolution type, failure category where applicable, manual intervention, total and recovery Rounds, and first-Round success. Keep integration facts separate from acceptance, and classify automatic completion only when its actual authority is recorded. Capture Skill failures and execution errors without mistaking every failed Skill attempt or automatic retry for final Goal failure.

Use shared work-item operations for CLI, API, browser and bulk decisions. Persist decisions and status atomically, fence stale or duplicate requests, preserve exact-candidate approval requirements, and retain earlier outcomes when work reopens. Keep this history through synchronization, log pruning and supported deletion or archival. Preserve original decision and completion timestamps and attribution; report unknown legacy data instead of inventing it.

Provide a shared query and CLI/API report over a date range, grouped by node, reporter or Feature, with time buckets, outcome counts, human accept rate, automatic resolution rate, first-Round success, average Rounds and failure rate. Define deduplication and denominators, expose missing-data coverage and use null for an empty denominator. Extend existing indexes and caches so routine queries do not scan every Round or run history.

Verify acceptance, rejection, Skill failure followed by recovery, cancellation, reopen, duplicate and stale submissions, sync conflicts, retention and legacy records. Check known fixture totals, rates, date boundaries and query performance.

This is a recovery Round following the Skills review on 10 September 2026. Start from current main in a new managed Round worktree. Preserve Round 1, its plans, logs, branches, commits and uncommitted files; inspect and selectively reuse useful work instead of replaying the whole old attempt. Use the current Skills and docs/intent contracts, not archived Governance, Quality or Guidance configuration or the old fixed planning sequence. Refine owns workflow advancement and integration; human approval remains separate. Update only affected documentation and report focused verification with actual results.

Implement acceptance and rejection with explicit reviewer identity and human decision provenance, existing acceptance proof requirements, locked revalidation of ownership, Review status, Round and exact candidate, and request identities that return the original event on identical retries while rejecting stale or contradictory submissions.

Route existing CLI, API, browser and bulk acceptance paths through the shared decision operation, add corresponding rejection actions and optional reasons, capture identity from explicit input or the selected acting reviewer, and keep automated review provenance distinct while preventing generic status changes from manufacturing human acceptance.

Capture terminal snapshots at every authoritative completion, cancellation and failure settlement, including bulk changes, process-stop failures, exhausted recovery and already-integrated recovery paths, preserving stale-worker and cancellation authority and recording exact integration and structured failure evidence before mutable failure fields are cleared.

Derive total_rounds from distinct recorded Rounds and recovery_rounds from explicit automatic or operator recovery lineage, mark required operator recovery or rejection as manual intervention while excluding ordinary final acceptance and automatic retries, and allow first_round_success only for successful first-Round completion without prior failure, rejection or required intervention.

Persist timestamped reopening and outcome supersession when undo, retry or a new Round resumes settled work, preserve every earlier decision and terminal snapshot unchanged, and distinguish separate settlements within one Round so recovery remains auditable without duplicating the current Goal outcome.

Preserve source updated timestamps during synchronization and no-op bulk operations, advance updated only for genuine Goal changes, and keep each event's decided_at and completed_at unchanged through metadata edits, transfer, projection refresh and reconciliation.

Extend existing persistence-sync merge and recovery rules to preserve the union of immutable audit entries by identity and their original timestamps and attribution, reject modifications to an existing event or incompatible lifecycle outcomes, and retain audit history through both automated and operator-authorized conflict resolution.

Retain decisions, terminal snapshots and lifecycle history outside runtime log and telemetry pruning, require durable synchronized archival retention before Goal or Feature deletion, and deduplicate archived and live copies by stable identities so deletion cannot erase or double-count metrics evidence.

Keep legacy Goal records readable without new fields, derive historical classifications and timestamps only from surviving durable evidence, and report unknown classifications and undated coverage separately without inventing human decisions or including unsupported records in attributed rates and time buckets.

Extend existing file-index and projection mechanisms with rebuildable decision and outcome indexes, incremental refresh after mutations and synchronization, and cached date and grouping aggregates so ordinary non-external metrics queries stay under 50 ms without scanning complete Goal histories.

Expose the shared metrics query through refine metrics and the API with machine-readable totals and UTC day, week or month buckets over an inclusive-start and exclusive-end date range, optional grouping by node, reporter or Feature, and attribution captured when each event occurred.

Count each Goal's latest unsuperseded terminal outcome as of the query end within the range by completed_at, count unique human decisions within the range by decided_at, calculate human accept rate as accepted divided by accepted plus rejected and auto-resolution, first-round-success and terminal-failure rates as their respective counts divided by classified terminal Goals, and report average total_rounds, explicit numerators and denominators, unknown coverage and null values for empty denominators consistently across totals, groups and time buckets.

Update only affected model, workflow, persistence-sync, CLI, API, Goal browser and Feature intent pages in their established format to describe durable review, Rejected, recovery history and metric definitions, keeping domain types, shared mutation policy, persistence projections and surface adapters within their existing responsibility boundaries.

previous_rounds.prompt:
From: Ethan Jacobson <ethan.jacobson@insurity.com>
Subject: Feature request: durable metrics for Goal resolution outcomes

Body:
CONTEXT / PROBLEM
We tried to measure how often Refine correctly resolves Goals and could not, because:
- There is no durable "Failed" or human-"Rejected" outcome. `done` is reached by auto-
  integration (Quality+Governance pass) OR by a human clearing the review queue - the two
  are indistinguishable after the fact.
- Human review decisions are not recorded: no actor, no timestamp, no accept/reject, no reason.
- The `updated` timestamp is overwritten by bulk state-sync (e.g. 15 Goals sharing one
  1-second timestamp), so approval time can't be recovered.
- Per-Goal execution logs are pruned to a rolling ~63-Goal window; failure history for the
  other ~1080 Goals is gone.
Net: we can compute "reached done" (95%) and "first-round resolution" (~72%), but NOT a real
human accept-rate or fail-rate.

WHAT WE NEED

1. Durable review-decision audit event, one per human accept/reject, never pruned:
   { goal_id, round, node_id, actor, decided_at, decision: accepted|rejected,
     reason (optional free text), candidate_commit }

2. Explicit "rejected" outcome distinct from `cancelled`. A QA person rejecting a candidate
   must be recordable as rejected (with reason), not disappear into cancelled/re-round/limbo.

3. Durable per-Goal terminal outcome, written at completion and never pruned:
   { final_status, resolution: auto_integrated|human_accepted|human_rejected|cancelled,
     failure_category (if failed), manual_intervention_required: bool,
     total_rounds, recovery_rounds, first_round_success: bool }

4. Preserve decision timestamps. Stop bulk-sync from overwriting `updated`; add a dedicated
   `decided_at` / `completed_at` that sync does not touch.

5. Query/report surface: `refine metrics` (or log export filters) that returns, over a date
   range and grouped by node/reporter/feature:
   - counts by resolution type (auto / accepted / rejected / cancelled / failed)
   - human accept rate = accepted / (accepted + rejected)
   - auto-resolution rate, first-round-success rate, avg rounds, terminal-failure rate
   - all as a time series (so trend over time is one command, not log-mining)

PRIORITY
(1)-(3) are the core: without a recorded, un-pruned accept/reject decision and terminal
outcome, no success metric is computable. (4)-(5) make it queryable and trendable.


[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Ethan Jacobson
Ethan.Jacobson@insurity.com

skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Inspect the repository and applicable context, resolve assumptions, consider alternatives and critique your proposed solution before finalizing it. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For a scoped finding recovery Round, focus the plan on the requested correction against the retained candidate. Do not change repository files. Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

checklist.description: Use the supplied Round 2 worktree throughout implementation and verification. Selectively reuse Round 1 outcome types, decision validation, archive handling and fixture ideas after reassessment; replace its automatic-completion inference and persistence hooks. Preserve the entire Round 1 worktree, branch, uncommitted files and historical artifacts. Leave integration, workflow advancement and serving-installation operations to Refine.

Add backward-compatible audit types in focused model/goal modules: immutable human decisions, terminal outcomes, recovery/reopening events and explicit completion authority. Decisions carry stable event/request identities, Goal, one-based Round, node, reviewer, original decision time, accepted/rejected result, optional reason and exact candidate. Outcomes capture completion time, resolution, failure category/evidence, intervention, Round counts and first-Round success. Capture Goal reporter and Feature attribution at occurrence time, independently of reviewer identity.

Add shared decision and settlement operations under application/work_items. Require request ID, explicit human provenance, reviewer and expected node, Round, candidate and revision/generation. Identical retries return the original receipt/event without changing timestamps; conflicting reuse and stale submissions fail without mutation. Commit decision, status, outcome and current-outcome reference in one durable Goal replacement under existing record locks and revision fencing. Validate immutable identities and causal references on every audit-bearing write.

Compose decisions with current Event transition gates. Persist a fenced pending request and original submission time when Skills defer a transition; expose pending separately from completion. Materialize the decision and terminal outcome atomically only when the transition actually settles, retaining decided_at and assigning completed_at at settlement. Deferred execution must revalidate ownership, revision, candidate and approval proof. Failed, cancelled or superseded gates retain request and Skill evidence without creating a completed acceptance. Never hold Goal locks while Skills execute.

Move review orchestration into the shared work-item capability and extract/reuse the existing integration-proof helper. Acceptance must retain successful exact-candidate integration, target ancestry and required publication checks, with proof and Goal identity fenced through final commit using established lock ordering. Rejection requires the reviewed exact candidate but does not need successful acceptance proof. Approval never integrates again. Generic status writes cannot create Done or Rejected without corresponding authorized evidence.

Add Rejected to workflow serialization, operations, projections, filters, browser presentation and the Skills trigger catalog. Rejected is settled, unsuccessful and unschedulable; like Failed, it holds ordered Feature work until explicit recovery. Preserve existing Review ordering behavior and Feature final-state rollup semantics while exposing rejected counts separately from successful completion. Support an explicit new Round from the current target after rejection, retaining integrated code and the rejection. Cancellation remains distinct.

Route CLI approval, API approve/verify aliases, browser actions and bulk acceptance/rejection through the same operation. Add rejection and optional reasons, use the selected acting reviewer or explicit CLI/API identity, and submit the candidate the caller actually reviewed. Bulk requests contain per-Goal identities and return individual completed, pending, stale and failed results. Preserve idempotency across browser reloads and transport retries; do not infer the reviewer from the Goal reporter or assignee.

Capture settlements at authoritative cancellation, process-stop failure, workflow-attempt failure, exhausted recovery and successful completion boundaries, preserving existing cancellation and stale-worker fences. Record Skill findings and execution errors using invocation/binding identities, candidate, timestamps and structured categories; retain compact durable evidence independent of process logs. Automatic retries and failed Skill attempts alone do not settle the Goal as Failed. Integration and no-required-Skills results remain check/integration facts. An existing configured automatic accept action must use shared proof validation and record its actual invocation, action and pinned configuration authority; otherwise no automatic resolution is classified.

Record immutable reopening/supersession events for undo, retry and new Rounds without modifying prior settlements. Count distinct Rounds; count recovery Rounds only from explicit successor lineage, excluding same-Round execution/output retries. Record required operator intervention separately from ordinary acceptance and automatic retry. First-Round success means successful resolution in Round 1 without earlier failed/rejected settlement, a recovery Round or required intervention. Preserve unknown historical lineage or intervention values rather than defaulting them to false.

Preserve original audit timestamps and attribution through metadata edits, transfer, synchronization and cache rebuilding. Keep current byte-preserving sync behavior and the existing top-level updated merge rule. Make unchanged bulk/status/metadata requests true no-ops; advance updated and revision for actual semantic changes, including Event receipts. Avoid Round 1's recursive removal of every field named updated when comparing records.

Extend application/persistence_sync validation across structural merge, fast-forward/hydration, agent resolution and live/remote recovery. Union independent immutable events by identity; reject same-ID payload changes, missing causal references and incompatible current settlements. Existing authority selection may settle current lifecycle through explicit reconciliation evidence but must retain both original histories. Validate archive coverage before publishing or applying deletion. Preserve ownership rules, retained refs and compare-and-swap publication.

Archive a Goal's audit and legacy coverage metadata in synchronized, inspectable durable state before supported Goal, bulk or Feature deletion. Make archive-before-delete restartable and idempotent; failed archival leaves the Goal present. Apply archives before dependent deletions during hydration. Keep decisions, outcomes, recovery lineage and required Skill summaries outside runtime retention. Deduplicate archive/live copies by event identity and preserve history across repeated archival, synchronization and reopening.

Extend existing project projections and Event indexes with compact decision, settlement, supersession and coverage entries, date/group lookups and bounded aggregate caches. Update incrementally after local mutations, Skill settlement, synchronization and archival. Use recoverable index-update markers/generations so a crash after a durable record write cannot silently serve stale totals. Rebuild missing/corrupt projections from durable records only as a recovery path; routine queries must not traverse Goal Rounds or invocation histories. Keep schema/derivation in Model, query policy in Application and storage mechanisms in Infrastructure.

Expose one shared query through refine metrics and GET /work/metrics using existing HTTP normalization. Support inclusive-start/exclusive-end UTC ranges, day/Monday-week/month buckets and node, Goal-reporter or Feature grouping. Default outcome counts use each Goal's unsuperseded settlement as of the exclusive end, included by completed_at; reopened unresolved Goals have no current settlement. Also return a clearly separate settlement-event series retaining earlier failures/rejections and recovery counts. Human decisions are independently deduplicated and dated by decided_at. Historical grouping uses captured attribution.

Define human accept rate as accepted decisions/(accepted+rejected decisions). Define automatic-resolution and terminal-failure rates over classified current terminal Goals in the selected window. Define first-Round success over that population with a known success flag, and average Rounds over records with known total_rounds. Return each numerator, denominator and excluded count; use null for empty denominators. Expose unknown classification, missing dates/attribution, incomplete recovery data and unresolved conflicts. Undated legacy records belong to explicitly unwindowed coverage, never invented time buckets; surviving integration evidence alone cannot establish human acceptance.

Add focused behavioral verification for immediate/deferred acceptance and rejection, exact-candidate proof, duplicate and contradictory retries, concurrent stale submissions, pending-gate cancellation, automatic authority, zero required Skills, Skill finding/error followed by recovery, terminal failure, cancellation, same/new-Round reopen, Feature ordering, sync conflicts and archive retention. Inject persistence/index/archive failures and restart between durable-write stages. Verify legacy readability, immutable timestamps/attribution, and browser/CLI/API/bulk parity. Place tests beside their cohesive responsibility rather than expanding existing large service files.

Verify known metrics with six classified final Goals: three human accepted, one authorized automatic, one failed and one cancelled; include an earlier rejection followed by acceptance and a Skill-failure recovery without terminal failure. Expect accepted/rejected decision counts 3/1, accept rate 3/4, automatic and failure rates 1/6, first-Round success 2/6 and average Rounds 8/6; the separate settlement history retains the earlier rejection. Add unknown legacy and duplicate archived copies without changing those denominators. Test boundary instants, offsets, leap/month/week boundaries, grouped totals and empty populations. Benchmark cold rebuild separately from warm and incrementally refreshed queries on at least 10,000 multi-Round Goals; instrument zero history-file reads on routine queries and measure against a 50 ms local-query target.

Update only affected intent pages for Goal history, Skills transitions, review/done/failed/cancelled/rejected behavior, persistence retention, CLI/API and Goal/Feature surfaces, including the metrics definitions. Verify from the pinned worktree with cargo check --all-targets --locked; cargo test --lib application::work_items -- --test-threads=1; equivalent separate filters for application::events, application::workflow, application::persistence_sync, application::projects::projection, model::workflow, model::feature and surfaces::web_server; cargo test --test sync_regressions --test sync_simulation -- --test-threads=1; and existing xtask test-cli/test-browser/check-static-assets commands. Finish with changed-file formatting checks and git diff --check. Report actual selected test counts, failures, skips, candidate identity and benchmark results; do not claim the proposed checks have already passed.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: The retained attempt predates Skills and cannot be replayed wholesale. P1 and P4 explicitly replace its transition integration while preserving useful source and all Round 1 evidence.
Inferring automatic completion from verified integration would manufacture authority. P8 requires the actual configured action and invocation, and excludes passing or absent checks from acceptance.

A generic persistence hook can misdate deferred completion or apply stale approval proof. P3-P5 distinguish pending request receipt from atomic decision settlement and revalidate at the deferred boundary.

Using only latest Goal outcomes hides recovered failures; counting all settlements as distinct Goals inflates final-resolution rates. P14-P15 expose separately named final-Goal and settlement-event populations with explicit denominators.

Round 1's full audit-map aggregation and timestamp-based cache identity do not establish routine query performance or crash consistency. P13 and P17 require indexed selection, recoverable invalidation and measured cold/warm behavior.
Blind whole-record authority selection or deletion can discard immutable history. P11-P12 validate retention on every publication/hydration route and make archival a prerequisite for deletion.

A log-derived report or separate authoritative database would undermine retention and architectural contracts. The plan keeps audit state with durable work items and synchronized archives, with disposable indexes owned by existing capabilities.
